evidence: The authors report: "The ranking of the relative importance of input parameters indicates that dust deposition is the most important factor influencing spatial bioavailable 87Sr/86Sr variation, followed by terrane age, soil clay content, maximum age of bedrock..." and later state "Geological variables also dominate in predicting bioavailable 87Sr/86Sr across Africa." However, they immediately corroborate these findings with partial dependence plots: "The partial dependence plots (Supplementary Fig. 3) reveal more radiogenic 87Sr/86Sr ratios occur in regions with low dust deposition." Their main conclusions center on predictive accuracy (R² = 0.84) and geolocation utility, demonstrated through case studies aligning with genetic evidence, not on the magnitude or ranking of feature importance.
